posts.name: schadkehnfreude
posts.cooked:
Got Near Mint but should've got Mint because I spaced out on something - but: even though it got quite hairy, I mostly had things in control, or as much in control as you can vs. Infinitor.

With the disclaimer that the decks will vary after shuffle effects and such a few turns in, the keys for me were:

- Cosmic Crest lets Capt. Cosmic tank the dudes that deal 4 energy damage to the highest HP hero.  Keep it alive at all costs.  Argent Adept made me goof up when Surprise Shopping trip came up (was trying to get Skyscraper to play a one-shot to nuke SST), but refrain from playing cards if you have to because if you keep Cosmic Crest and its buddies out, it makes things super easy.

- Argent mostly gave Sky extra card plays - his opening hand sucks but you get alactrious subdominant after turn 1

- Skyscraper does a little bit of everything - have her get Chrono the Masdah ASAP - that and compulsion canisters will be your primary source of damage.  I never got Monolith in my game, fwiw.

- Immediately after Fixed Point shows up, Heroic Infinitor plays a one-shot that plinks everything for 1 damage.  This is your best window to win:  If the one-shot resolves without burying all manifestations he will play a few more dudes and you're going to have a bad time.  Therefore, the turn BEFORE is when you gotta get all the manifestations below zero.  If Sky and Chrono are doing their thing you should have enough damage to make that happen.  Where I goofed was there was so many manifestations that I didn't scroll all the way to the right and missed out on a 4 hp manifestation that I could easily have hit.  Also, don't be afraid to buff Heroic Infitor with Syncopated as well to make sure the manifestations go under him.  (I can't remember offhand if it was Throne or Shopping Trip that's your cue that Fixed Point/Whispering Madness(?) is next)

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Minty fresh, everyone around 12 or 13 HP (except Sky-Scraper, because she ate a bunch of damage from Thorathian Monolith). AA, well, I've had worse draws. Skipped his first turn to get Alacritous Subdominant out quick, then used it to help set everyone else up (Proportionist helped a ton), then swapped it out for Syncopated Onslaught to buff Infinitor and Chrono Ranger. I did end up focusing on CR -- he got Masada out and a Dynamic Syphon, which helped tag-team Surprise Shopping Trip (I got Monolith out before it came up, had AA put a Temporal Grenade out for CR, then had SST hit the Dynamic Syphon first so CR could just nuke it).

I didn't see Compulsion Canister until after Sky Scraper's last turn, and Captain Cosmic nuked all his constructs to bring the last Manifestation down before Fixed Point came out.

All in all, wasn't too bad -- but gorram, am I learning to hate Infinitor's (both versions) DR.

posts.name: JimmyTheCannon
posts.cooked:
Got a Mint! Nice to get one again.

I really wasn’t sure what to do with AA’s opening hand. Didn’t get much use with him early on. CC got Cosmic Crest out early to tank the energy damage, and Sky-Scraper helped Crono get the Masada out early. He really came into his own once he got Hunter and Hunted, Compound Bow, and two bounties out.

The normally terrifying Ocular Swarm manifestations were just punching bags, good targets to leave for last as they did nothing. The “2 energy 2 psychic” ones were only a minor danger to the constructs, as two of them would take one out. The bigger problem was the “3 Fire damage to the two highest HP targets”, which kept hitting both Infinitor and CC.

The Surprise Shopping Trip was a big problem. No damage to the manifestations but plenty to everyone else. Sky-Scraper took it out with Emergency Evac.

I blew a chance to wipe out a manifestation with Catch a Ride, but it turned out fine, as Infinitor then played Whispers (or whichever card he has that hits all targets for one) and I believe chained into a second one and cleared all the manifestations for the win.

posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked:
Arcanist Lupus:

Hey, does anybody think that it's possible to win before Infinitor plays his last card?  I've played around a little, but I haven't managed to do it.

It's possible. You have to use Sky-scraper's Neutralizing Resonator in order to do it, though. The bottom of Infinitor's deck is stacked like this (bottom card listed is last card played):

Crazed Artifice
Whispers of Oblivion
Crazed Artifice
Lambent Reaper
Recalescent Hellion
Whispers of Oblivion

What happens is Crazed Artifice reveals Whispers of Oblivion and the next three cards, discarding the Whispers of Oblivion and playing the two Manifestations. In order to get Whispers of Oblivion to be played instead of discarded, you must discard Crazed Artifice, the only means of which is via Neutralizing Resonator on the proper turn. (The turn in question is the round where he just plays Ocular Swarm, fyi).

I managed to win by Infinitor's fourth turn by utilizing Neutralizing Resonator twice, on rounds three (discarding Lambent Reaper) and four (discarding Crazed Artifice). If you were to play Neutralizing Resonator in the first round, then theoretically it's possible to win on Infinitor's third turn, since his card then would be Whispers of Oblivion, but I'm not sure whether that's possible.
